episodes.title: The Name Before the Man
episodes.script:
SFX: [en] Subscription hall erupting—boots, angry shouts, reporters calling questions.
EWAN: [en] Ada! Look at me. Tell them who emptied your shop.
ADA: [en] Keep away from me, traitor.
GREGOR: [en] Mr Pell, the lady has answered you before witnesses.

SFX: [en] A gavel hammered against wood.
COMPERE: [en] The second Briarhaven subscription remains open. Eighty pounds at issue.
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] Is she truly the state printer?
ADA: [en] I hold the commission and the Green Cross.
EWAN: [en] You taught me that a printer names the type, the stock and the press. Name them now.
ADA: [en] I do not submit to examinations from deserters.
EWAN: [en] Which press printed the bonds?
GREGOR: [en] Mr Pell, must your humiliation become repetitive?
INES: [en] Ewan, she is frightened.
EWAN: [en] She is precise when she is frightened.
ADA: [en] Ask my father’s account where the missing letters went.
SFX: [en] A metal printer’s sort drops and rings on the floor.
GREGOR: [en] Enough. Escort Miss Wren upstairs. Gently, gentlemen. She is an officer of state.
ADA: [en] The wrong letters always leave an impression.
SFX: [en] A door slams above; a key turns.

SFX: [en] Crowd thinning, coins counted into wooden trays.
EWAN: [en] Let me speak with her alone.
GREGOR: [en] No.
EWAN: [en] Then produce her commission register and her father’s account.
GREGOR: [en] You crossed an ocean to accuse me of lacking registers. Now you demand two more. Persistence can resemble character from a distance.
EWAN: [en] You bought her father’s debt.
GREGOR: [en] Debt is not bought, Mr Pell. It is relieved by a more patient creditor.
EWAN: [en] Where is her father?
GREGOR: [en] At liberty, provided his daughter continues to behave with professional dignity.
EWAN: [en] And the print shop?
GREGOR: [en] Consolidated. Idle machinery is a sorrowful thing.
INES: [en] Let her leave with us.
GREGOR: [en] Madam, London rewards those who recognise its doors. That one is not yours.
EWAN: [en] Ada was taken because you held her father’s debts.
GREGOR: [en] Miss Wren accepted an appointment. If you insist on using uglier words, perhaps ask why her father is not in a debtor’s cell.
EWAN: [en] I am asking her.
GREGOR: [en] Tomorrow, if she signs the third printing order, she may answer any appropriate question in my presence.
EWAN: [en] There will be no third order.
GREGOR: [en] A charming ambition. Your mother’s account has been discharged, I hear. That makes courage much cheaper.
SFX: [en] Gregor’s cane taps away across the boards.

SFX: [en] Narrow stairwell—pipes knocking, a guarded door rattling overhead.
ADA: [en] Ewan?
EWAN: [en] One minute. Tell me the truth.
ADA: [en] They purchased every note against my father. Rent, paper, ink, the Albion press. One hundred and twelve pounds.
EWAN: [en] Who purchased them?
ADA: [en] A private account controlled by Gregor. The men came before opening, emptied the shop and brought the plates here. They said my father would be arrested before noon unless I came with them.
EWAN: [en] Why accuse me today?
ADA: [en] Each public appearance removes ten pounds from his account. Each refusal restores twenty.
EWAN: [en] Come down now.
ADA: [en] There are two guards and my father’s signed confession is in Gregor’s desk.
EWAN: [en] Confession to what?
ADA: [en] Counterfeiting every Briarhaven instrument. If I run, they file it.
EWAN: [en] I can take the plates.
ADA: [en] Plates prove one workshop. The master ledger proves who ordered every sheet and received every payment.
EWAN: [en] Where?
ADA: [en] Records room. Iron cupboard. Lower lock sticks after the second turn.
EWAN: [en] The key?
ADA: [en] They searched me.
SFX: [en] Fingernail scraping wax from beneath a stair rail.
ADA: [en] I pressed it here when they took my bag. The wrong letters leave an impression.
GUARD: [en] Who is below?
ADA: [en] A traitor begging forgiveness.
INES: [en] Then let us disappoint him elsewhere.
SFX: [en] Ewan and Ines hurry down the stairs as the guard’s bolt draws back.

NARRATOR: [en] The subscription hall closed at eleven. Gregor left by the front entrance with three investors and two reporters. Ewan returned through the coal hatch.

SFX: [en] Coal scraping; iron hatch lowering softly.
INES: [en] You said you knew this building.
EWAN: [en] I know the documents. Buildings are less orderly.
INES: [en] The guard turns every seven minutes. We have five.
EWAN: [en] I need the ledger and Ada’s father’s confession.
INES: [en] You may carry one book quietly. Choose before the guard chooses for you.
SFX: [en] Footsteps overhead; a distant key ring.
EWAN: [en] Records room should be beyond the certificate press.
INES: [en] Should be?
EWAN: [en] The floor plan was printed in a Briarhaven prospectus.
INES: [en] Then it may contain a cathedral.
SFX: [en] A latch lifts; door opens.

SFX: [en] Printing workshop—rollers ticking as they cool, paper rustling in a draught.
EWAN: [en] Ada’s press.
INES: [en] And the shop’s type cases.
EWAN: [en] Constitution headings. Bank charter border. Military commissions. All here.
INES: [en] Do not prove what we already proved. Find the cupboard.
SFX: [en] Heavy footsteps approaching beyond the room.
EWAN: [en] Iron door, left wall.
SFX: [en] Wax mould pressed around a key blank; lock resists.
EWAN: [en] First turn.
SFX: [en] Lock clicks, jams.
EWAN: [en] Second turn. It is stuck.
INES: [en] Ada said after the second turn.
EWAN: [en] I heard her.
INES: [en] Your shame is loud enough without speaking it.
SFX: [en] Ewan forces the key backward a fraction; the cupboard opens.
EWAN: [en] Master subscription ledger. Land grants, bonds, recruiting receipts—indexed by purchaser.
INES: [en] Take it.
EWAN: [en] Wait. A leaf has been cut out near the front.
INES: [en] We have forty seconds.
EWAN: [en] Ada’s father’s confession is not here.
INES: [en] Then Gregor keeps it closer.
SFX: [en] Door handle tested from outside.
GUARD: [en] Records room?
INES: [en] Now, Ewan.
SFX: [en] Ledger shoved beneath a coat; cupboard closes.

SFX: [en] Coal hatch bursts open; street cart rattling past.
GUARD: [en] Stop there!
SFX: [en] Running footsteps, whistle blasts, cart wheels splashing through a gutter.
INES: [en] Into the alley!
EWAN: [en] The book is tearing my coat.
INES: [en] Better the coat than your neck.
SFX: [en] They turn sharply; pursuing boots continue past.

SFX: [en] Cellar door barred; ledger dropped onto a packing crate.
INES: [en] Read enough to know we stole the right one.
EWAN: [en] First bond issue. Seven hundred subscriptions. Elspeth’s recruiting payments. Cyrus’s validation fee.
INES: [en] And Gregor?
EWAN: [en] Private withdrawals beside every institutional payment.
SFX: [en] Pages turning faster, then stopping.
INES: [en] What is it?
EWAN: [en] The ledger contains a payment to me dated two weeks before I was supposedly hired.

episodes.title: The Price Before the Paper
episodes.script:
SFX: [en] Exchange bell clanging; brokers shouting prices over one another.
EWAN: [en] Silas! Before you sell another bond, explain why Gregor paid me before he hired me.
SILAS: [en] Not here.
EWAN: [en] Here. Before the exchange crowd.
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] The traitor has brought an account book!

SFX: [en] Brokers crowding closer, pencils scratching.
SILAS: [en] Close that ledger, Ewan. Paper survives men who speak carelessly beside it.
EWAN: [en] Entry dated before my appointment. Twenty-five pounds under my name. I never received it.
SILAS: [en] Then you have saved twenty-five pounds by doing nothing. Many investors envy you.
EWAN: [en] Who entered it?
SILAS: [en] A clerk.
EWAN: [en] Which clerk?
SILAS: [en] One with excellent handwriting and poor prospects.
EWAN: [en] Gregor placed advance commissions under the names of clerks he intended to hire, did he not?
SILAS: [en] I move instruments. I do not baptise them.
EWAN: [en] He entered money under my name before I arrived so every later fraud would appear to begin with my paid consent.
SILAS: [en] You have crossed the ocean and returned with a taste for conclusions.
EWAN: [en] Deny it.
SILAS: [en] I decline to improve your performance.
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] Did Pell take the money or not?
SECOND VOICE: [en] Ask him about the dead settlers!
EWAN: [en] I took no payment before my employment. Silas knows the entry was planted as an advance commission against a clerk Gregor had not yet recruited.
SILAS: [en] Keep your voice down.
EWAN: [en] That is the first honest instruction you have given me.

SFX: [en] A hand snatches at the ledger; leather cover slams against a railing.
SILAS: [en] Give me that book.
EWAN: [en] No.
SILAS: [en] It belongs to the Briarhaven administration.
EWAN: [en] Then name the lawful officer who will claim it.
SILAS: [en] Do not play a clerk’s game with me.
EWAN: [en] Entries, dates and signatures are the clerk’s game. You only profited because no one asked the clerk to read them aloud.
SFX: [en] Exchange bell strikes again.
COMPERE: [en] Briarhaven second issue offered at eighty-two!
BROKER: [en] Eighty-one!
ANOTHER BROKER: [en] Seventy-nine!
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] Let him read!

EWAN: [en] On the fourteenth of April, the loan was publicly validated at two hundred thousand pounds.
SILAS: [en] Everyone here heard it.
EWAN: [en] You told me that day that seven hundred certificates had already been subscribed or reserved.
SILAS: [en] Demand was considerable.
EWAN: [en] You also said the unprinted bonds issued at eighty pounds were trading at eighty-six.
SILAS: [en] A strong market is not a crime.
EWAN: [en] How were bonds traded before the certificates existed?
SILAS: [en] By subscription receipt.
EWAN: [en] Secured by what?
SILAS: [en] The forthcoming loan instruments.
EWAN: [en] Forthcoming. Not existing.
SILAS: [en] Timing is not falsehood.
EWAN: [en] When did Cyrus first receive the loan certificates he claimed to validate?
SILAS: [en] Ask Cyrus.
EWAN: [en] I am asking the broker who sold them.
SILAS: [en] And I am refusing the unemployed clerk who stole a private ledger.
EWAN: [en] Then refuse me under oath.
SFX: [en] Crowd reacts; several canes knock against the floor.
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] Yes! Under oath!
SECOND VOICE: [en] Answer the date!

SFX: [en] A walking stick taps twice; the crowd quiets unevenly.
CYRUS: [en] This exchange is not a courtroom. Mr Pell’s distress is understandable after his unfortunate expedition, but an account book removed at night proves only theft.
EWAN: [en] Did you independently validate the first bond issue?
CYRUS: [en] My bank examined the instruments submitted to it.
EWAN: [en] Did those instruments exist before Silas sold subscriptions against them?
CYRUS: [en] Commercial arrangements frequently precede engrossment.
EWAN: [en] Seven hundred certificates were subscribed or reserved. At eighty pounds each, that is fifty-six thousand pounds committed before the paper existed.
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] Fifty-six thousand?
CYRUS: [en] Committed is not paid, and a reservation is not a sale.
EWAN: [en] Silas called them sold when the price rose to eighty-six.
SILAS: [en] I said they were trading.
EWAN: [en] Then tell these men what they traded.
SILAS: [en] Expectation.
EWAN: [en] Whose expectation?
SILAS: [en] The market’s.
EWAN: [en] Built on Cyrus’s validation.
SILAS: [en] Yes.
EWAN: [en] Given before the certificates existed.
SILAS: [en] No.
EWAN: [en] Then state the date you delivered the certificates to his bank.
SFX: [en] Nothing. Long.
EWAN: [en] State it.

CYRUS: [en] Silas, there is no obligation to indulge him.
SILAS: [en] You said the file was complete.
CYRUS: [en] It was complete for the purpose required.
SILAS: [en] You said your signature covered the interval.
CYRUS: [en] This is neither the place nor the audience for private recollection.
EWAN: [en] The date, Silas.
SILAS: [en] The certificates reached the bank on the sixteenth.
EWAN: [en] Two days after the validation.
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] He validated blank paper!
ANOTHER VOICE: [en] We bought before the bank received anything!
CYRUS: [en] You bought subscription rights supported by a sovereign undertaking.
EWAN: [en] There was no recognised sovereign government. I stood at the supposed capital. There was no harbour, no parliament and no resident official.
CYRUS: [en] Your travel account remains contested.
EWAN: [en] Silas’s date is not.
SILAS: [en] I did not say the paper was blank.
EWAN: [en] You said the certificates arrived two days after Cyrus validated them. Say the rest plainly.
SILAS: [en] Why?
EWAN: [en] Because men in this room paid real money for paper you had not printed.
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] My family bought four!
SECOND VOICE: [en] I paid three hundred and twenty pounds!
EWAN: [en] Say it before them.
SILAS: [en] The first Briarhaven bonds were sold before the promised loan certificates existed.
SFX: [en] The exchange erupts—angry shouts, desks struck, the quoted price called downward.
BROKER: [en] Briarhaven at sixty-eight!
ANOTHER BROKER: [en] No buyer at sixty-eight!
VOICE IN CROWD: [en] Perring, answer him!

SFX: [en] Cyrus’s stick cracks against a desk.
CYRUS: [en] Mr Lowe has confused printing with legal creation. His commission depended upon volume, and excitement has made him imprecise.
SILAS: [en] My commission depended upon money reaching both of you.
CYRUS: [en] Think carefully.
SILAS: [en] I have. Markets forgive greed. They do not forgive the last man left holding it.
EWAN: [en] What else do you have?
SILAS: [en] Protection.
EWAN: [en] From whom?
SILAS: [en] Whoever loses first.
SFX: [en] Small keys pulled from a chain; a dispatch box opens beneath a broker’s desk.
CYRUS: [en] Close that box.
SILAS: [en] You called my recollection private. Let us improve it with figures.
SFX: [en] A second ledger lands open on the exchange desk.
EWAN: [en] Whose accounts are these?
SILAS: [en] Cyrus’s commissions. This ledger shows he received money from both the bank and Gregor’s private account.

episodes.title: Protection in Confidence
episodes.script:
SFX: [en] Government carriage door opens amid a hostile crowd outside the exchange.
ROBERT: [en] Mr Pell, enter the carriage if you prefer protection to arrest.
EWAN: [en] Protection from whom?
ROBERT: [en] That depends upon which door reaches you first.

SFX: [en] Crowd pounding the carriage panels; horses moving off.
VOICE OUTSIDE: [en] Pell! Where is our money?
ANOTHER VOICE: [en] Arrest Perring!
ROBERT: [en] You have produced an inconvenient morning.
EWAN: [en] Silas admitted the bonds were sold before the loan certificates existed.
ROBERT: [en] I heard. Half the exchange heard. By luncheon, the sentence will have acquired six versions and a death toll.
EWAN: [en] One hundred and fifty-nine survivors entered Crownwater Colony. The first ship carried one hundred and seventy-three settlers.
ROBERT: [en] Give me the master ledger, the duplicate plate and the boundary evidence. Quietly.
EWAN: [en] No.
ROBERT: [en] You misunderstand the offer.
EWAN: [en] You offered a closed door.
ROBERT: [en] I offered government protection, immunity from prosecution for document offences and secure lodging for your mother.
EWAN: [en] In exchange for silence.
ROBERT: [en] In exchange for orderly evidence. Silence is such an emotional word.
EWAN: [en] The families were sold a harbour that does not exist.
ROBERT: [en] And shouting that fact through London will not build one.
EWAN: [en] It may stop the next ship.
ROBERT: [en] That is already being considered.
EWAN: [en] Considered by whom?
ROBERT: [en] By men who do not announce policy from exchange railings.
SFX: [en] Carriage blinds snap shut.

NARRATOR: [en] The carriage did not stop at a police office. It entered a government courtyard where no creditor was permitted to follow.

SFX: [en] Iron gates closing; carriage wheels halt on stone.
ROBERT: [en] Bring the ledger. Leave the plate concealed unless asked.
EWAN: [en] You know I have it?
ROBERT: [en] Mr Pell, a clerk carrying nothing does not hold his coat with both hands.

SFX: [en] Office door opens; coal fire, papers shifted across a broad desk.
ROBERT: [en] Sit.
EWAN: [en] I will stand.
ROBERT: [en] Then we shall both pretend that grants you leverage.
SFX: [en] A document box unlocks.
ROBERT: [en] Crownwater transmitted an examination summary. No harbour. No public buildings. No resident officials. No functioning Briarhaven government.
EWAN: [en] Then you know the survivor testimony is true.
ROBERT: [en] I know an administrator recorded it.
EWAN: [en] Edwin fed the survivors and admitted them as distressed passengers.
ROBERT: [en] A careful classification. It avoids recognising the state they believed they had entered.
EWAN: [en] Because Briarhaven is not a state.
ROBERT: [en] Recognition is a tool, not a reward for honesty.
EWAN: [en] Gregor is preparing more certificates. Ada is confined above his subscription hall because he holds her father’s debts.
ROBERT: [en] Can she testify freely?
EWAN: [en] Not while he holds a signed confession over her father.
ROBERT: [en] Then she is presently a compromised witness.
EWAN: [en] She is a prisoner.
ROBERT: [en] Again, an emotional word where a useful one is available.
EWAN: [en] What useful word do you have for one hundred and seventy-three people sent to jungle and ruins?
ROBERT: [en] Exposure.
EWAN: [en] Whose?
ROBERT: [en] Ours, if handled badly.

SFX: [en] Master ledger placed on the desk.
EWAN: [en] Every bond, land grant and recruiting payment is indexed here. Cyrus took commission from his bank and from Gregor’s private account.
ROBERT: [en] This could collapse the second issue.
EWAN: [en] It should collapse the first one too.
ROBERT: [en] The first issue has already changed hands. If it is declared fraudulent today, innocent holders lose before the architects do.
EWAN: [en] They have already lost.
ROBERT: [en] They possess a negotiable claim.
EWAN: [en] Against what?
ROBERT: [en] That is the question your evidence makes dangerous.
EWAN: [en] Dangerous to investors or to the government?
ROBERT: [en] Must we choose?
EWAN: [en] Yes.
ROBERT: [en] Then I choose the order in which they are informed.

SFX: [en] Cabinet drawer slides open; sealed dispatches rustle.
EWAN: [en] What is that order?
ROBERT: [en] Future vessels will be intercepted before they reach the Sable Coast.
EWAN: [en] You have issued it already.
ROBERT: [en] A draft has advanced beyond discussion.
EWAN: [en] Where will the passengers be taken?
ROBERT: [en] Crownwater Colony where practical. Other safe ports where necessary.
EWAN: [en] When will you warn them in Britain?
ROBERT: [en] We will not announce the interception yet.
EWAN: [en] Then recruiting continues.
ROBERT: [en] Temporarily.
EWAN: [en] Families will still sell homes, buy land and board ships.
ROBERT: [en] Ships we intend to stop.
EWAN: [en] After the money is taken.
ROBERT: [en] A public warning would destroy the bonds before the government identifies the full exposure of British banks.
EWAN: [en] So investors receive silence and settlers receive interception.
ROBERT: [en] Settlers receive life. Investors retain the possibility of value while inquiries proceed.
EWAN: [en] There is no value. The capital has no harbour, buildings or officials.
ROBERT: [en] Your certainty is admirable. Government must survive certainty.
EWAN: [en] How many ships are expected?
ROBERT: [en] Three are under discussion. One may sail within days.
EWAN: [en] And you will let passengers pay until the gangway is raised.
ROBERT: [en] We will prevent them reaching the false settlement.
EWAN: [en] Without telling them why.
ROBERT: [en] Without causing a commercial panic that may consume firms entirely unconnected with Gregor.
EWAN: [en] Cyrus’s bank is connected.
ROBERT: [en] Your second ledger suggests that. A hearing must establish it.
EWAN: [en] Publicly.
ROBERT: [en] Privately first.
EWAN: [en] No.

SFX: [en] Chair pushed back sharply.
ROBERT: [en] Consider your position. You engraved a seal, certified land and prepared bonds. Gregor will say you designed the mechanism.
EWAN: [en] His ledger planted a payment under my name before I was hired.
ROBERT: [en] Which makes you appear involved earlier, not later.
EWAN: [en] Silas can explain the entry.
ROBERT: [en] Silas will explain whichever version preserves Silas.
EWAN: [en] The survivors know what I did at the coast.
ROBERT: [en] Survivors know hunger. Courts know signatures.
EWAN: [en] Is that the protection you offered?
ROBERT: [en] It is the danger from which protection would be useful.
EWAN: [en] I will testify in public. I will name the bonds, the plates, the missing government and every payment in that ledger.
ROBERT: [en] Then the Office cannot prevent interested parties from describing you as the author of the alarm.
EWAN: [en] I am the source of evidence, not the author of the fraud.
ROBERT: [en] Documents are less sentimental about distinctions.
EWAN: [en] Show me the interception order.
ROBERT: [en] That is not part of our arrangement.
EWAN: [en] There is no arrangement.
SFX: [en] Ewan snatches a dispatch; wax seal skids across the desk.
ROBERT: [en] Put that down.
EWAN: [en] It orders Crownwater and neighbouring ports to intercept every vessel carrying Briarhaven settlers.
ROBERT: [en] Continue to the authority line.
SFX: [en] Paper unfolds once more.
ROBERT: [en] The government dispatch names Ewan Pell as the official source, making him liable for every death and every lost investment.

beat_sheet.location: London subscription hall and guarded stairwell
beat_sheet.what_happened: Ada covertly told Ewan that Gregor controlled her through her father's debts and had moved the print shop's machinery and plates into the Briarhaven office.

state_changes.fact: learned why Ada disappeared and publicly accused him
her coercion through her father's £112 debt became known to Ewan

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan and Ines entered the Briarhaven office after closing and recovered the master ledger connecting land grants, bonds and recruiting payments.

state_changes.fact: obtained the master Briarhaven ledger
lost exclusive control of its central financial record

beat_sheet.what_happened: An unidentified person removed a leaf from the front section of the master ledger before Ewan recovered it.

state_changes.fact: has a missing leaf of unknown contents

beat_sheet.note: The removal had no identified witness; Ewan later discovered only the cut edge, leaving the actor and contents as deliberate open canon.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan found a payment recorded under his name in the master ledger two weeks before his supposed hiring date.

state_changes.fact: was implicated by a ledger payment predating his employment

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan confronted Silas publicly with the master ledger and Silas's knowledge that Gregor had recorded advance commissions under prospective clerks' names.

state_changes.fact: learned that the pre-employment payment was planted to imply prior complicity
was forced to answer publicly from the operation's records

beat_sheet.what_happened: Silas publicly admitted that the first Briarhaven bonds were sold before the promised loan certificates existed.

state_changes.fact: lost its claim of prior independent validation before the exchange crowd
secured a public admission supporting his accusation
admitted the premature sale before investors and brokers

beat_sheet.what_happened: The exchange crowd heard that £56,000 in subscriptions or reservations had been committed before the bank received the certificates, and the quoted Briarhaven bond price fell without a buyer at sixty-eight.

state_changes.fact: public market confidence collapsed after Silas's admission
his institutional validation was publicly challenged with a specific delivery date

beat_sheet.what_happened: Silas produced a second ledger showing that Cyrus received commission money from both the bank and Gregor's private account.

state_changes.fact: was documented as receiving commissions from both sides of the validation
gained documentary evidence against Cyrus's independence

beat_sheet.location: government carriage and Colonial Office, London
beat_sheet.what_happened: Robert offered Ewan protection, immunity and secure lodging for Mara in return for quietly surrendering the master ledger, duplicate plate and boundary evidence.

state_changes.fact: received an official offer of protection conditioned on private disclosure
sought control of Ewan's evidence before public proceedings

beat_sheet.what_happened: Robert disclosed that the Colonial Office intended to intercept future Briarhaven settler vessels without warning British investors or prospective passengers first.

state_changes.fact: planned maritime interception without an immediate public investor warning
learned that rescue policy was being separated from public disclosure

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan refused Robert's private protection arrangement and declared that he would give the evidence publicly.

state_changes.fact: rejected official protection in favour of public testimony
lost Ewan's cooperation with a private evidence process

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan read a government interception dispatch naming him as the official source and assigning him liability for deaths and lost investments.

state_changes.fact: was officially named as the source bearing liability for the Briarhaven warning
linked the interception policy and its consequences to Ewan by name

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Where was Ada taken, and why did her father's print shop disappear overnight?
promise_ledger.how_paid: Ada told Ewan that Gregor purchased £112 of her father's debts, moved the shop's presses and plates into the London office, and compelled her to serve by threatening her father with arrest.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Why does a Briarhaven boundary marker predate Gregor's claimed acquisition of the territory by three years?
Why is Ada wearing the Green Cross and publicly accusing Ewan of abandoning Briarhaven?
promise_ledger.how_paid: Ada revealed that each coerced public appearance reduced her father's debt while refusal increased it and exposed him to a counterfeiting charge.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Why does the master ledger record a payment to Ewan before he was hired?
promise_ledger.how_paid: Silas's exchange confrontation established that Gregor recorded advance commissions under prospective clerks' names so later fraud would appear to begin with their paid consent.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Who removed the missing leaf from the front of the master ledger, and what did it contain?
Can Ewan free Ada while Gregor holds her father's signed counterfeiting confession?
What did Cyrus provide in return for receiving commissions from both the bank and Gregor's private account?
How can Ewan expose Briarhaven after the government dispatch makes him officially liable for the consequences?

dates_fixed.what: Ewan certifies the sixty-acre grant at the public Edinburgh presentation.
Ewan compares the institutional papers, attempts to resign, and is shown Mara's debt ledger.
The packed recruiting-hall sale takes place and Ewan finds the duplicate banknote serial number.
Ewan and Ada prove the papers came from one workshop; the following morning Ewan finds the shop emptied and Ada missing.
Cyrus validates the £200,000 loan, Ewan prepares certificates, and the first settler ship departs Northhaven.
Ewan begins his journey under a false name, reaches the Sable Coast after six weeks, inspects the capital site and finds the 1831 boundary marker.
A hurricane strands the settlers and the northern trading post rejects Ewan's sealed requisition.
The 159 surviving settlers enter Crownwater Colony and Edwin records Ewan's public testimony.
Six weeks after the Crownwater rescue, Gregor launches the second London bond issue and presents Ada as Acting Superintendent of State Printing.
Ewan learns why Ada is being coerced, enters the Briarhaven office after closing and recovers the master ledger shortly after midnight.
